input:
Labeled defect
- root cause: Argument.get_help_record returns self.help unchanged, so the second element of the tuple is None for an undocumented argument even though format_arguments now feeds every record straight into formatter.write_dl without a fallback.
- failure path: A command declares two arguments and sets help on only one; running it with --help makes write_dl measure and wrap a None description and the help command crashes with a TypeError instead of printing usage.

Reviewer finding
- description: The positional-arguments help section now passes Argument.get_help_record() rows straight to write_dl, but that method returns (metavar, None) when the argument has no help text. The old `or (metavar, "")` fallback that covered this case was removed.
- rationale: Trigger: a command with one positional argument that has help and another positional argument with no help, so help is None. Any help output then reaches write_dl with a None description. The formatter is expected to wrap a string there, so it likely raises (for example AttributeError) or renders incorrectly. Impact: `--help` crashes or prints a broken Positional arguments section for such commands, which are common.
critique: The finding names the same mechanism: get_help_record returns (metavar, None) for an argument with no help text, the fallback was removed, and the None goes into write_dl, so --help crashes when one argument has help and another doesn't. The exception type it guesses differs (AttributeError instead of TypeError), but that does not change the defect.
